results.claim: The recorded target is dimensionally inconsistent: literal ISO A9-in-A1 has optimum 258, so it is neither 518 nor 519.
results.proof_sketch: The supplied table gives A1 dimensions 594×841 and A9 dimensions 37×52. Thus the container area is 499554 and each A9 has area 1924. In particular, 260·1924=500240>499554, so even the area bound is 259. The 518/519 dichotomy instead matches 26×37 A10 rectangles, since 519·962=499278≤499554<520·962. Both interpretations are settled in the following claims.

results.claim: OPT(594,841,52,37)=258, with an explicit placement and a periodic upper-bound certificate.
results.proof_sketch:
Placement: split the width as 37+37+260+260. In each 37-wide strip stack sixteen 37×52 rectangles (height 832). In each 260-wide strip put four 52-high rows containing seven 37×52 rectangles each, followed by seventeen 37-high rows containing five 52×37 rectangles each. These use height 4·52+17·37=837 and give 28+85=113 rectangles per wide strip. The total is 2·16+2·113=258.

For the upper bound, arbitrary real-coordinate packings may first be floored coordinatewise. Integer side lengths preserve containment, and every pair's separating-axis inequality remains valid after flooring. Mark x-coordinates whose residues modulo 37 lie in X={2,9,16,24,31}, and y-coordinates with residues in Y={5,12,19,27,34}. Give a unit cell weight 1/35 exactly when both its coordinates are marked. Each residue set has cyclic gaps 7,7,8,7,8. Hence every 37 consecutive coordinates contain five marks, while every 15 contain at least two, so every 52 contain at least seven. Every 37×52 or 52×37 rectangle therefore contains at least 5·7=35 weighted cells and has weight at least one. There are 80 marked container columns and 113 marked rows, so the total weight is 80·113/35=258+2/7<259. Thus every packing contains at most 258 rectangles.

results.claim: If the intended 518/519 instance is ISO A10-in-A1, its exact optimum is 518.
results.proof_sketch:
Placement: split the width as 74+520. In the 74-wide strip, stack 32 rows of two 37×26 rectangles, giving 64. In the 520-wide strip, use fifteen 37-high rows of twenty 26×37 rectangles and eleven 26-high rows of fourteen 37×26 rectangles. Their total height is 15·37+11·26=841 and their count is 300+154=454. Altogether this packs 518.

For the upper bound, apply the same coordinate-flooring reduction and mark coordinates with residues R={2,6,10,14,17,21,25,28,32,36} modulo 37. Weight a unit cell 1/70 when both coordinates are marked. Every 37-coordinate interval has ten marks. The cyclic gaps are 4,4,4,3,4,4,3,4,4,3; any three consecutive gaps sum to at least 11, so an 11-coordinate interval contains at most three marks. Consequently every 26-coordinate interval, whose complement in a 37-cycle has length 11, contains at least seven marks. Each 26×37 rectangle therefore contains at least 7·10=70 marked cells. The container has 160 marked columns and 227 marked rows, giving total weight 160·227/70=518+6/7<519. Hence 519 is impossible and the optimum is 518.

final_writeup:
Let C=[0,594]×[0,841]. The supplied ISO table makes the literal A9 dimensions 37×52, so the stated 518/519 alternatives cannot apply: the literal optimum is exactly 258. Indeed, the source table associates the 258–259 bound with A9-in-A1 and the 518–519 bound with A10-in-A1.

The unit-grid certificates below apply even when arbitrary real coordinates are allowed. Replace every rectangle's lower-left corner (x,y) by (⌊x⌋,⌊y⌋). Because all side and container lengths are integers, containment is preserved. For every pair of interior-disjoint rectangles, at least one separating inequality holds, for example x_i+w_i≤x_j. Flooring preserves it because ⌊x_i⌋+w_i=⌊x_i+w_i⌋≤⌊x_j⌋. Thus every real-coordinate packing yields an integer-coordinate packing of the same cardinality.

A checkable 258-placement is given parametrically as follows:

• For s∈{0,1} and k=0,…,15, place [37s,37(s+1)]×[52k,52(k+1)].

• For X∈{74,334}, k=0,…,3, and c=0,…,6, place [X+37c,X+37(c+1)]×[52k,52(k+1)].

• For the same X, k=0,…,16, and c=0,…,4, place [X+52c,X+52(c+1)]×[208+37k,208+37(k+1)].

The three families contain 32, 56, and 170 rectangles. Their strip and band structure makes interior-disjointness immediate, and their largest used coordinates are x=594 and y=837.

For the matching upper certificate, on the 594×841 unit-cell grid mark columns modulo 37 in {2,9,16,24,31} and rows modulo 37 in {5,12,19,27,34}; assign weight 1/35 at intersections and zero elsewhere. Every A9 placement receives weight at least one, while the entire container has weight 9040/35=258+2/7. Therefore the literal ISO A9 answer is 258.

The numerical alternatives 518 and 519 instead correspond exactly to ISO A10 dimensions 26×37. That corrected instance also has a complete answer: 518. A placement uses a 74-wide strip containing 32 rows of two 37×26 rectangles, and a 520-wide strip containing fifteen rows of twenty 26×37 rectangles followed by eleven rows of fourteen 37×26 rectangles.

Its upper certificate marks both coordinate axes at residues {2,6,10,14,17,21,25,28,32,36} modulo 37 and assigns weight 1/70 at marked intersections. Every 26-coordinate interval has at least seven marks and every 37-coordinate interval exactly ten, so each A10 rectangle has weight at least one. The total is 36320/70=518+6/7<519. Thus, under the evident dimension correction, the requested choice is 518.
